sections.html:
Lebanon County keeps its land records in Room 107 of the Municipal Building at 400 South 8th Street, Lebanon, PA 17042. Call 717-228-4447. The office is staffed Monday through Friday, opening at 8:30 in the morning and closing at 4:30 in the afternoon.

Everything that touches title to land in the county gets filed here: deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, easements, plans, UCC financing filings and notary bonds. A seller meets this office twice. The deed from the old owner to you was recorded here when you bought, and the deed you sign at closing goes onto the same record. If a mortgage is paid off from your sale proceeds, the lender's satisfaction piece also lands on the county record, usually a few weeks after the payoff.

Staff will help you find a record, but they won't tell you how to word a deed or whether a name should come off one. The office is a custodian of records and sends those questions to an attorney.

A standard deed or mortgage costs $91.75 to record under the fee schedule that took effect November 12, 2025. That base price covers up to four pages and four names, and it already contains the affordable housing fee, the records improvement fee, the parcel identifier fee and the court and access-to-justice surcharges, so those don't show up as separate line items.

A few smaller charges can matter on a sale:

  • A Statement of Value that has attachments adds $2.00 for each attachment page. The duplicate copy for the state carries no charge.
  • Sending a document by email to the office costs $5.00 plus $0.50 for each page.
  • A returned check costs $30.00.
  • Copies run $0.50 per page on sheets up to tabloid size, and oversized pages add $5.00.

The office takes cash or checks only. Write the check to the Recorder of Deeds for the exact amount, because fees and transfer taxes are due when the document is presented.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before it is recorded
sections.html:
The deed must show a Uniform Parcel Identifier, called a UPI, on page one, and the county Assessment Office must certify that number. The certification happens electronically inside the courthouse. If you don't have the number, call Assessment at 717-228-4425 or use the county property viewer to look the parcel up by address.

The recording instructions add several other requirements:

  • A signed certificate of residence for the grantee on every deed, and for the mortgagee on every mortgage or assignment.
  • Type no smaller than 10 point, and a legal acknowledgment before a notary.
  • A typed English translation attached to any document written in another language.
  • Page numbers or numbering that shows the filing order when several documents belong to one transaction.
  • Where a parcel straddles two or more municipalities or school districts, the percentage lying in each, so the local levy can be split.
  • A return envelope, addressed and stamped, big enough to carry the originals home.

A Statement of Value, the state's REV-183 form, is filed in duplicate with its attachments. It is required when the deed doesn't state the full price, when the transfer is a gift or has no consideration, when an exemption is claimed, and when the property was sold at a tax claim or sheriff sale. A statement isn't needed when full consideration is paid, when the transfer is between close family members, or when the grant is an easement to a public utility. Fill in every block, sign it, and date it with the settlement or acceptance date.

The state's realty transfer tax is 1 percent of a property's value, paid at the counter with the filing fee. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue holds grantor and grantee jointly responsible. A local levy rides on top, divided between the school district and municipality that cover the house. Call the office or your settlement agent to learn the combined percentage for your street address.

Exemptions cover some family transfers, inheritance by will or intestacy, and government transfers. Anyone claiming one must lay out the basis on the REV-183. The Statement of Value also shows Lebanon County's common level ratio, 1.39 percent.

In a typical sale the settlement agent works out the tax and delivers a check. The purchase agreement says which side absorbs the cost.

Most filings are back with their owners the next business day, by pickup, mail or electronic return. Each document is received, reviewed and keyed in, sent to Assessment to certify the UPI, returned for recording, and then proofread. Documents are recorded in the order they arrive, so a heavy day can lengthen the wait.

Electronic recording is accepted through Simplifile, CSC and ePN, and confirmation can come back in minutes. A mailed filing needs a check for the exact amount plus the return envelope.

Landex, the county's records vendor, also runs record alerts tied to a parcel number. If you own a rental house or a home left empty after an inheritance, ask the Recorder of Deeds how to sign up.

Documents recorded from 1925 to the present can be searched online through Landex. Anything older has to be viewed at the office in Room 107. Anyone may view the records, with one exception: military discharge papers (DD214 forms) are kept private. They can be recorded for free.

Phone help is limited, because the office isn't insured for title searching. Plan to do your own search online, or hire a title company if the chain of ownership is complicated. A deed describes the land and not the buildings on it, so adding a house to a lot doesn't produce a new deed.

Notary commissions are handled in the same office. The notary fee is $42.00, which includes the Prothonotary fee, paid by one check payable to the Recorder of Deeds.

Lebanon County has an estimated 146,380 residents for 2025, up from 143,257 in 2020. Whether a house sits in Lebanon city, a borough such as Palmyra, or a township changes which municipality and school district receive the local transfer tax, so confirm your municipality before you estimate closing costs.

faqs.q: What is the base deed fee in Lebanon County?
faqs.a: Under the schedule effective November 12, 2025, the base fee is $91.75 and covers up to four pages and four names. Each extra page costs $4.00 and each extra name $1.00. The county accepts cash or check only.

faqs.q: Does Lebanon County require a parcel number on a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The Uniform Parcel Identifier belongs on the first page and must be certified by the Assessment Office. Call 717-228-4425 to get the number for your property.

faqs.q: Can I record a Lebanon County deed by email or mail?
faqs.a: Mail works with an exact-amount check and a stamped envelope for the return. Email submission is accepted for $5.00 plus $0.50 per page, and electronic recording through Simplifile, CSC or ePN is also available.

faqs.q: How soon will my recorded deed come back?
faqs.a: Most documents are returned the next business day. The wait depends on how many documents were filed ahead of yours, since the office records in order of arrival.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a Lebanon County sale?
faqs.a: Seller and buyer both answer to the state for it, and the tax is payable at the counter at filing. The sales contract decides who bears the cost in practice, so check it with your closing agent.
